2027-01-24.title: Kohne Sunday · Commemoration of the Departed Priests
readings: Aaron anointed for an everlasting covenant
Paul's farewell to the elders of Ephesus
2027-01-24.alt: Kohne Sunday: the Church remembers the priests who have died. St Francis de Sales is also remembered today.
2027-01-24.verse: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
theo: Before the Great Fast the Malankara Church keeps two Sundays of remembrance. The first is Kohne Sunday, the commemoration of the departed priests (kohne in Syriac). We remember the bishops and priests who baptised us, taught us, absolved our sins, celebrated the Holy Qurbono for us, and buried our dead. Hebrews tells us: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.”

The readings recall the death of Israel's great servants. Aaron, the first high priest, dies on Mount Hor, and Moses places his vestments on his son Eleazar (Numbers 20:28): the priesthood continues though the priest dies. Joshua dies after leading the people into the land. Sirach remembers Aaron anointed “for an everlasting covenant… to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name” (Sirach 45:15).

In Acts Paul says farewell to the elders of Ephesus: “Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.” And he reminds them of the Lord's words: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” The Gospel asks the question every priest will be asked: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time? Blessed is that servant whom his master will find at work when he arrives.”

We pray today for the departed priests, that the Lord who called them may forgive their weaknesses and say to them: “Well done, good servant!” (Luke 19:17). And we pray for our living priests, and for new vocations. “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever” (Hebrews 13:8): priests pass, but the one High Priest remains.
conn: Aaron's garments placed on Eleazar (Numbers 20:28): the priesthood does not die with the priest. In the Church the one priesthood of Christ continues through every generation.
Luke 19 and Matthew 24: priests are stewards, not owners; they will give an account.
Acts 20 is the model of a pastor's last words: I did not shrink from declaring the whole purpose of God; I coveted no one's silver or gold.
Hebrews 13:8–16: Christ the same yesterday, today and for ever; our sacrifice of praise continues his.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono offered today in the world is offered by hands that will one day be still. Through them the one Priest, Christ, offers his one sacrifice. Today we offer the Qurbono for the priests who once stood at this altar for us.
outline: Name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you, buried your parents.
Gratitude for the priests who served us.
Aaron's vestments on Eleazar: Christ's priesthood outlives every priest.
The faithful and wise servant: a word for priests and for every Christian steward.
For the departed, for the living, for vocations.
live: Pray by name for the priests who served your family, living and dead.
Tell your parish priest one thing you are grateful for.
Pray daily for one young person from your parish to answer God's call.
fathers: On the priesthood: the priest stands at the altar as a minister of heavenly things; the dignity is great, and so is the responsibility, for he will answer for the souls entrusted to him (On the Priesthood III).
The good shepherd is known by his care for the flock: he must be near to each by compassion and above all by contemplation (Pastoral Rule II).
magis: Priests share in the priesthood of Christ; taken from among the people, they are set apart for the people, to offer sacrifice and forgive sins in Christ's name.
The ministerial priesthood is at the service of the common priesthood; the priest acts in the person of Christ the Head.
The Church prays and offers the Eucharistic sacrifice for the dead.
saints: 25 Jan: the Conversion of St Paul; the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity ends. 26 Jan: Republic Day of India. 28 Jan: St Thomas Aquinas. 31 Jan: St John Bosco.
2027-01-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal High Priest, we remember before you the bishops and priests who served your people and have gone to their rest. Forgive their weaknesses, reward their labours, and give them a place of light. Keep our living priests faithful, and raise up new labourers for your harvest. Amen.

quick: Kohne Sunday: we remember the departed priests.
The priesthood continues: Christ is the one High Priest.
“Remember your leaders and imitate their faith.”
2027-01-24.action: Pray by name for the priests who served your family.
2027-01-24.question: Which priest helped my faith most, and how can I thank God for him?
2027-01-24.special: Kohne Sunday, commemoration of the departed priests.
illus: In many Kerala parishes the tombs of former vicars lie near the church door. On Kohne Sunday the people light candles there after Qurbono. Some of those priests baptised the grandparents of today's children.

family.explain: Priests bring us Jesus in the Holy Qurbono and in Confession. Today we thank God for priests who have died and pray that they are happy with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the priests who have died, for our parish priest, and for new vocations.
family.ask: Ask: “Which priest baptised each of us? Let us pray for him.”

catechism: Purification after death and prayer for the dead.
kidsaint: A priest in Turin who gathered poor boys from the streets, taught them a trade, played with them and led them to Jesus. Lesson: priests are fathers who care for us; pray for them.
term: Kohne is Syriac for “priests”. The first of two Sundays of remembrance before the Great Fast: departed priests (Kohne) and all the departed faithful (Aneede); then the Fast begins with Kothine (Cana) Sunday.
termMore: Before entering the Great Fast, the Church remembers her dead: it is a reminder that Lent is a journey towards Easter, the victory over death.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, eternal High Priest, today we remember the priests who served your Church and have gone before us. Receive them into your joy, and bless us as we pray. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders… and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Which priest's faith do I want to imitate?
The faithful and wise servant (Matthew 24:45). How faithful am I in the tasks God has given me?
Paul commended the elders of Ephesus to God and to the message of his grace (Acts 20:32). How do I support my parish priest?
interc: For all departed bishops and priests of our Church.
For the priests who baptized us, taught us and absolved us.
For living priests, especially those who are tired, sick or lonely.
For our group, that we may be faithful servants.
pm.close: Father, you gave your Church shepherds after your own heart. Grant rest to those who have died, and strengthen those who serve today. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Kohne Sunday, when our Church remembers the priests who have died. Think for a moment of the priests in your own life: the one who baptised you, who gave you your First Holy Communion, who heard your confessions, who blessed your marriage, who buried your parents. Many of them are now with the Lord.

The letter to the Hebrews says: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” We remember them with gratitude. They were human, with weaknesses like ours, but through their hands Christ gave us his Body and Blood and his forgiveness.

Our reading from Numbers tells how Aaron, the first high priest, died, and Moses placed his vestments on his son Eleazar. The priest dies; the priesthood continues. For Christ is the one eternal High Priest, “the same yesterday and today and forever”. And the Gospel asks every priest one question: were you a faithful and wise servant, giving God's household their food at the proper time?

Today let us offer this Qurbono for our departed priests, that the Lord may say to them: “Well done, good servant.” Let us thank and support our living priests. And let us pray that from our families God may call new priests, to stand at this altar when we are gone. Amen.
kids: Children, who baptised you? A priest! Who gives you Jesus in Holy Communion? A priest!
Today we remember priests who have died and gone to Jesus. We thank God for them and pray that they are happy in heaven.
Let's pray for our parish priest too. Maybe one day God will call one of you to be a priest or sister! Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for our priests!”

intro: Theme: “Remembering the priests who served us.”
On Kohne Sunday the Church remembers her departed priests. We thank God for them, we pray for them, and we reflect on the gift of the priesthood that continues among us.

sub: On Mount Hor Moses took Aaron's vestments and put them on Eleazar: the ministry continues after death.
Every priest is taken from among the people and appointed for the people, to offer gifts and sacrifices.
The priests who baptised us, absolved us and fed us with the Eucharist have handed on Christ's priesthood to the next generation.
q: Moses stripped Aaron of his vestments, and put them on his son Eleazar; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain.
Every high priest chosen from among mortals is put in charge of things pertaining to God on their behalf, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
points.apply: Remember by name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you or buried your loved ones.

points.h: Faithful stewards of the Master's gift
sub: Aaron was anointed to minister to the Lord and bless the people in his name.
In the parable of the pounds, the faithful servant is praised for trading with what he received.
Priests are judged by faithfulness, not success; so are all of us in our vocations.
q: Moses ordained him, and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and for his descendants … to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name.
He said to him, “Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.”
points.apply: Encourage a priest this week with a word of thanks, and pray for one who is struggling.

sub: Judas Maccabeus offered sacrifice for the dead, “a holy and pious thought”.
The Church prays for the faithful departed, that they may be purified and enter God's rest.
Our prayers and Holy Qurbono offered for departed priests are an act of gratitude and charity.
q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
Blessed are the dead who from now on die in the Lord. “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds follow them.”
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered, or pray a Rosary, for a departed priest.

concl: The priests we remember today gave their lives so that Christ might be present among us.
Let us thank God for them, pray for their eternal rest, and pray that the Lord will send good and holy priests to his Church.
2027-01-24.resolve: Visit the grave of a priest in your parish cemetery and pray for him.
